verdict: Approved. I looked at the corrected page PDF 206 (printed 198) and compared it with the earlier render. The colliding '12[8/9]' marks are now one readable '128,129' mark that touches no other text. Both footnotes are still complete and in order: 128 is the Hebrew note on the continuation headings (PDF 262-272) and 129 is the English 'Repeated printed continuation headings…' note (PDF 263-273). The prayer text on the page matches the earlier render: the Thou wilt make idols disappear row, the 'As it is written…' row, The Lord will be King, Shema, the separator, Elohenu ve'Elohei avoteinu meloch, the אם שבת bracket and Sanctify us. Each row is in the same Hebrew/English pairing and position, and the running head and page number are unchanged. The machine evidence is taken as reported, not recomputed by me. The 60dpi raster comparison of all 226 pages shows only PDF 206 changed, inside the marker box. The TeX diff changes only the two visible labels and keeps apparatus 128 and 129. The documentary-hebrew and expanded TeX files are byte-identical. The hardening pass leaves all three TeX files unchanged. The exporter review approves the code and the 375 passing tests. The refreshed artifact report shows no outside-page boxes, missing glyphs, overfull hboxes or undefined references. The other PDFs and all HTML are unchanged, so the earlier visual approval still covers them. This closes the only blocking finding from the first review. Its cosmetic findings and the source and encoding limits still stand: the first-day volume and all nine volumes remain incomplete, and nothing is claimed about the source leaves that follow.
